target_customer: Job seekers, especially students and early career, paying a monthly plan for automated applications
problem: Applying to jobs means retyping the same resume data into dozens of forms. Candidates want matching, tailored applications and tracking done for them.
business_model: Consumer subscription by application volume ($19, $39, $99 per 30 days; first 25 free)

founders.name: Agnay Srivastava
education: Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology, CS and AI, class of 2026
founders.background_notes: Per YC page. NewsBytes reports he was 21 at the time of the funding story, not at founding.

founders.name: Pulkit Gupta
education: Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology, CS, class of 2028
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; built a language app with 1M+ downloads at 17.

competitors.name: LazyApply
competitors.what: High volume auto apply Chrome extension for LinkedIn and Indeed

competitors.name: Jobright
competitors.what: AI job agent sourcing, tailoring and applying

competitors.name: Simplify
competitors.what: Autofill and application tracking without auto submit

competitors.name: AIApply
competitors.what: Auto apply plus interview prep, credit priced

technical_complexity.rationale: Submitting across 30+ ATS platforms and many career pages needs robust browser automation and resume tailoring; hard parts are reliability and anti-bot defenses.

defensibility.rationale: Many auto apply tools already existed and the approach is easy to copy; price and volume are the main levers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established auto apply tools were already selling; one roundup reports Sonara shut down, from a competitor blog and unverified.

market_need_then: Job seekers face high application volume. The founders applied to over 3,000 jobs by hand. Company claims 90,000+ users and about $3M annualized in three months, which conflicts with the launch post figure of 45,000+ users.

identity.voice_and_tone: benefit led: AI career agent on your side

branding.community_and_virality: Student founder story covered by Rose-Hulman, NewsBytes and YourStory; publishes comparison blog posts against rivals.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive invented name with student founder press, but no evidence of community, merch or word of mouth beyond growth claims.

outcome_analysis: Tsenta is an active Summer 2026 YC company founded by two Rose-Hulman students who report quick consumer growth. The auto apply market was already crowded and easy to copy, so durability depends on interview outcomes and retention. No outcome exists yet.
notes: The $500K is the YC deal as reported by Rose-Hulman and NewsBytes (Rs 5 crore); stage set to other because sources do not label it. Batch conflict: Tsenta's own AI disclosure page says W25, YC lists S26. User and revenue claims conflict across sources. Competitor listings come from a rival vendor blog.
